lead.headline: Supreme Court rules that converts to Islam cannot claim backward class reservation on the strength of their old caste
lead.byline: THE WEEK · ANI · THE HINDU · 15 OCT
lead.short: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Madras High Court ruling that struck down a Tamil Nadu order letting converts to Islam from backward castes be counted as Backward Class Muslims. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar dismissed the state's appeal. Conversion does not make someone a member of a notified backward community, the court held.

why.text: The ruling limits how states can extend caste quotas to converts, a question that also hangs over Dalit Christians and Muslims across India.

more: Tamil Nadu's 2024 order said converts from Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes, denotified tribes or Scheduled Castes could be treated as BC (Muslim). The High Court quashed it on 25 June. The case began with Sameer Ahamed, who converted in 2015 and asked to be certified as a Muslim Lebbai, one of the seven Muslim communities on the state's backward list.
DMK chief M.K. Stalin asked the TVK government to seek a review. "Social backwardness does not arise in a day or a generation," he said. "Conversion to another religion does not erase it."
The judgment does not touch the separate question of Scheduled Caste status for Dalits who convert, which is before a commission.

seconds.headline: School roof collapse in Peshawar kills at least 27 children and a teacher
seconds.short: At least 27 pupils under the age of 13 and one teacher died when the roof of an elementary school collapsed in the Afridi Abad area of Peshawar on Thursday, officials said. More than 40 others were taken injured to Lady Reading Hospital, and rescuers were still searching the rubble for children.

why.text: It is the deadliest of a run of school collapses in Pakistan this year, blamed on poor building standards and maintenance.

more: "We have taken out at least 45 children," said the district emergency officer, Iftikhar Khan, adding that more were thought to be under the rubble. A teacher told reporters from her hospital bed that the building had three floors and more than 1,200 pupils and staff.

Such collapses have become frequent. In July three girls were killed near Umerkot when a government school's outer wall gave way, and a child died in Lahore when the roof of an unfinished private school fell in. A month earlier 14 children died in a tutoring centre in Lahore, shortly after another collapse in Dera Ghazi Khan.

seconds.headline: Government sells control of IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax for about $5.5 billion; the shares fall 7%
seconds.short: The government and LIC are selling a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings of Canada for about $5.5 billion, one of India's biggest financial-sector deals. IDBI shares fell about 7% on Thursday. The deal shows how overseas investors are seeking a foothold in one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, Bloomberg says.

why.text: It jump-starts the government's push to reshape state banking and opens the door to more foreign buyers in Indian finance.

more: The stake is split between the Centre, about 30.5%, and LIC, about 30.2%. The sale still needs the Reserve Bank's fit-and-proper approval of Fairfax, clearance from the competition regulator and an open offer to minority shareholders.

Bloomberg says the deal helps start the government's push to reshape banking, with policymakers weighing fewer and larger state lenders. Foreign deals in Indian financial services came to about $20.5 billion last year; Blackstone is said to be eyeing IIFL Finance, and Japan's MUFG is studying control of Shriram Finance.
Analysts expect more stake sales, partnerships and capital-raising deals in the sector as wealthier Indians and a growing middle class lift earnings.
The shares had risen 9% on Tuesday as the announcement neared.

seconds.headline: Madrid come from 3–1 down to beat Roma 4–3, with Espí, Endrick and Rüdiger scoring off corners
seconds.short: Real Madrid won 4–3 at the Olimpico on Wednesday night after trailing 3–1 with less than half an hour left. Mbappé scored first, Donyell Malen twice put Roma ahead, and substitutes Carlos Espí and Endrick headed in from corners before Antonio Rüdiger scored the winner. Mourinho took the blame for the first hour.

why.text: Two wins from two in the group, but the defending was poor again three weeks before the Clásico, which Vinícius will now miss.

more: Roma opened with four long shots and led through a strike from outside the area that beat a diving Courtois. Mbappé equalised with a clever turn before half-time. Malen made it 2–1 with a deflected shot and then 3–1 after being played onside. Mbappé had a goal ruled out for offside.

Mourinho brought on Güler, Bernardo Silva, Espí and Endrick and moved Valverde to right-back, and the game turned. Diomande, switched to the left, set up a goal and led the match in dribbles and interceptions. Rüdiger, who scored the winner, also made a game-high seven clearances.
Madrid play Sevilla at the Bernabéu on Sunday.

update.front: A comeback from two goals down in Rome is the result of Madrid's season so far.

seconds.headline: Anthropic tells investors its revenue rose 45% to $16.8bn in a quarter as it prepares to list; AI chip stocks tumble
seconds.short: Anthropic, maker of Claude, told prospective investors on Wednesday that its revenue rose 45% to $16.8bn in the July to September quarter, the BBC reports, and that it made a profit for a second quarter running. It is preparing a stock market listing, expected before the end of the year.

why.text: The listing would be the first test of what public investors will pay for a leading AI lab, just as markets are doubting the AI spending boom.

more: Revenue has risen every quarter this year, from $4.7bn in the first three months to $11.6bn in the second. The briefing was held at the company's San Francisco headquarters. Bloomberg described the growth as slowing, which some investors read as a warning for the AI trade.

Chip shares fell sharply the same day after Broadcom's chief executive, Hock Tan, questioned AI spending at a conference on Monday. On Thursday South Korea's Kospi and Kosdaq were halted after falling more than 8%, with Samsung down 9.5% and SK Hynix 11%. Japan's Nikkei lost close to 5% and SoftBank more than 9%.

update.new: Revenue rose 45% to $16.8bn in the quarter, with a second profitable quarter.
update.front: The first figures given to would-be shareholders landed on the day AI chip stocks crashed across Asia.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks the Centre to explain its prohibitory orders and alleged police assaults on protesters
stories.short: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices on petitions against the Delhi Police's handling of the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, asked the Centre why it imposed prohibitory orders, and ordered CCTV footage preserved, including from the court's own premises. The CJP has called a 'Lehra Do Tiranga' gathering at Connaught Place on Friday.

why.text: The court is now examining how the protests were policed, not only what the protesters want.

more: The bench sought replies on allegations that police assaulted protesters, lawyers and journalists. The Solicitor General said no journalists' devices had been seized; the court told him to say so in his affidavit. Lawyers' bodies said the Police Commissioner should apologise.

The court is also hearing Rahul Gandhi's petition seeking the files and notings of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on the voter-roll revision, which has deleted about 13 crore names. The Youth Congress has challenged the closing of Jantar Mantar in the Delhi High Court.
The CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in judicial custody until Monday.

update.new: The Supreme Court issued notices and ordered CCTV footage preserved.

facts.sc: notices issued; CCTV to be preserved

stories.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries and accuses the US of cutting intelligence and slowing Starlink
stories.short: Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times that Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after holding off for three days at Washington's request while Russia kept hitting Ukraine's power grid. He accused the US of withholding intelligence on incoming Russian attacks and said a slowdown of Starlink was deliberate. "We're done," he said.

why.text: A split between Kyiv and Washington over the war changes the odds of a ceasefire and of more Russian oil on world markets.

more: Zelensky said US officials told Kyiv: "if you will not stop [the strikes], we will block intelligence". Ukraine relies on US early warnings to set up its air defences. Trump denied halting intelligence-sharing. Elon Musk appeared to deny that the Starlink slowdown was a technical fault, pointing at the Trump administration. "It was not a technical problem, it was the will," Zelensky said.
He had said he would accept Trump's "energy ceasefire" if Moscow did, but says Russia ignored it within hours. The Kremlin never agreed to it.
Sweden's prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, criticised the US deal to buy Russian diesel as a step "in the wrong direction".

update.new: Ukraine will resume refinery strikes; Zelensky accuses the US of cutting intelligence.

facts.us: intelligence and Starlink cut, Zelensky says

briefs.text: Since 1972 a second has been added every few years to keep clocks in step with the Earth's slowing, wobbling spin. Dropping it would let atomic time drift slowly away from the sun's.

stories.headline: Shai Hope's hundred and Keemo Paul's five wickets beat India by 24 runs; the series goes to Bengaluru at 2–2
stories.short: West Indies made 247 in Hyderabad on Wednesday, with captain Shai Hope's unbeaten century his fourth in seven matches on the tour, and won by 24 runs. Sanju Samson hit a 20-ball fifty but Keemo Paul took five wickets. The five-match series is 2–2, with the decider at the Chinnaswamy on Saturday.

why.text: India's bowling has now conceded 247 and 249 in two defeats, and the last match is in Parth's city.

more: Jewel Andrew hit Arshdeep Singh for two fours and a six early, and West Indies made 79 in the powerplay, the joint-highest against India in T20Is. Arshdeep and Mayank Yadav gave away 104 runs in eight overs between them; Axar Patel went for 22 in one over to Rovman Powell.

"It all started with bowling. I think we didn't execute our line lengths well," said India's captain, Shreyas Iyer. Samson called Tilak Varma's dismissal the turning point. Former India batter Mohammad Kaif said on Cricbuzz: "You will never win the World Cup with this combination."
Samson also became the sixth Indian to hit 100 sixes in T20Is.

update.new: West Indies won the fourth match to level at 2–2.
